text:
micah: Heads-up — a customer hit a crash when using the JS SDK in Cloudflare Workers. stacktrace shows `require('http')` and `fs` missing. they were running the default npm bundle.

tanvi: yeah Workers don't have Node built-ins. Did they bundle the CJS node-target build by accident? :grimacing:

micah: looks like it. also observed our retry logic tries to re-open sockets which obviously fails. crash happens during auth signing because we call `crypto.createHmac` (node-only).

ben: Repro: I tried the same with a minimal worker and confirmed. The bundle pulled `node-fetch` style codepath in the SDK. We should detect edge runtime and expose a tiny edge entrypoint that uses WebCrypto + global fetch.

carla: +1. We have three problems: 1) runtime detection/exports, 2) crypto shims (HMAC), 3) retry/keepalive semantics and streaming compatibility. Also TS types: consumers on Workers use lib.dom, not lib.node, so `Buffer`/`ReadableStream` types differ.

micah: Proposal: add a lightweight `edge` entrypoint in package exports and a minimal runtime shim that: uses `globalThis.fetch`, uses `crypto.subtle` for signing, and avoids Node-only APIs. Keep it un-opinionated: don't polyfill `fs` or process.

ben: Example conditional exports snippet I prototyped (for discussion):

```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "default": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs",
    "browser": "./dist/edge/index.mjs"
  }
}
```

carla: Works for bundlers that respect `browser` or `exports`. For CF Workers using native ESM, they import the bundle URL directly. We should also publish a tiny `@redwood/inference-edge` package for zero-config.

tanvi: For auth: WebCrypto example to replace Node HMAC (this is short but workable):

```js
// edge-hmac.js
async function hmacSha256(keyBytes, dataBytes) {
  const key = await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', keyBytes, { name: 'HMAC', hash: 'SHA-256' }, false, ['sign']);
  const sig = await crypto.subtle.sign('HMAC', key, dataBytes);
  return new Uint8Array(sig);
}
```

micah: Nice. Also need to tweak our retry: Workers don't have sockets/keep-alive; retries should assume idempotency based on method and rely on `Accept-Ranges`/idempotent headers where possible. And streaming: our existing ReadableStream usage assumed Node streams; in Workers we should use WHATWG streams.

ben: On TS, suggestion: ship a separate `dist/edge/index.d.ts` and use conditional exports for `types` so consumers on `lib.dom` get correct declarations. Practically, we can add a `types` export entrypoint via `package.json` exports (some tooling supports it) or publish `@redwood/inference-edge` with its own types.

carla: Action items:
• micah: RFC PR that defines the `edge` API surface + minimal shim and runtime checks (should include code snippet for runtime detection)
• ben: prototype `crypto.subtle` adapter and `fetch`-only http client (no agent)
• tanvi: test matrix: bundler edge case (wrangler, vite, esbuild), native Workers ESM import, and Cloudflare Pages Functions
• carla: doc on onboarding: how to pick edge vs node package and examples

micah: runtime detection snippet I use in the prototype:

```js
function isCloudflareWorker() {
  return typeof WebSocket === 'undefined' && typeof globalThis?.caches === 'object' && typeof globalThis?.fetch === 'function' && typeof globalThis?.crypto?.subtle === 'object';
}
```

ci-bot: CI:edge-tests pipeline queued for branch `edge-sdk-shim` — 3 jobs

tanvi: One more caveat: streaming responses in Workers are locked down — e.g., you can't pipe a Node stream. We should provide `response.body.getReader()` helpers and examples in sample apps.

micah: Agreed. Let's avoid automatic polyfills that bloat bundles. Prefer: small edge-specific package or conditional exports + clear docs. I'll open the RFC and link the prototype later in the thread.

carla: thanks — if anyone hits blockers trying the prototype ping me. :thumbsup:

ben: I'll paste a minimal example worker app in the RFC showing fetch + hmac usage and a retry wrapper that uses a simple idempotency key pattern.

micah: perfect. closing loop once RFC PR lands.
